provenance.warning: A LIVE CAPTURE PROVES MORE THAN A HAND-BUILT SAMPLE, BUT IT IS STILL THE HAPPY PATH. This account is owned by the ACTING BANKER, and both endpoints scope reads to the caller. A banker reading a CUSTOMER's account behaves differently and asymmetrically: get_account returns 404 (loud - evidence missing, propose refuses) while list_account_transactions returns 200 with an EMPTY ARRAY (silent). The projection would then assert {accountId, count: 0, items: []} - 'this account has no transaction history' - when the truth is 'the banker cannot see them'. count: 0 is present and non-null, so EvidenceComplete PASSES and the approval record carries a false statement. This sample cannot detect that, and neither can the seam test. Deferred deliberately (Brian, 2026-09-08); named before `main`. It also does not prove the shape is stable - only that it was true at capture time.

supersededByRuling.status: STALE PROVENANCE — SHAPE SURVIVES, PATH DOES NOT. The response body, the projection and the resulting shape are unchanged by that ruling, so the Gate B seam tests remain valid and are not blocked. But this was captured AS BANKER AGAINST A BANKER-OWNED ACCOUNT, and after the ruling the product no longer takes that path: the banker owns nothing and reads a CUSTOMER's account. A fixture captured on a path that no longer runs is a measurement of a configuration nobody runs.
supersededByRuling.behaviourDescribedInWarningNoLongerExist: The `warning` above describes the pre-ruling behaviour and is retained as the record of the defect, not as a description of the shipping product. A banker reading a customer's account now succeeds; a caller with no authority is refused 403 by both endpoints; and an empty array from list_account_transactions now means the ledger is empty and nothing else.
